name: @effectified/material-web
tagline: inherited properties read from its types, a form and a dialog

decisions.question: Which exported functions and classes does the facade offer?
decisions.why: none: a frontend facade offers its elements as Effect UI bindings; the exported classes are those elements' constructors (MdSwitch, Switch, ...), which an app never calls, and the UI generator reads elements, not exports

decisions.question: Which upstream failures become which tagged errors?
decisions.why: kept: @material/web exports no error classes and the facade wraps no calls that fail; the catch-all is unused by the UI generator

decisions.question: Which handles are provided as services (Context.Service with a layer)?
decisions.why: kept: a frontend facade offers no handles

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-filled-field>?
decisions.why: an internal building block: the text fields and selects render it in their shadow roots; it is not documented for apps and owns no input of its own

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-outlined-field>?
decisions.why: an internal building block: the text fields and selects render it in their shadow roots; it is not documented for apps and owns no input of its own

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-focus-ring>?
decisions.why: documented for custom components (attach it to a control with `for` or `control`); a stable element

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-ripple>?
decisions.why: documented for custom components (attach it to a control with `for` or `control`); a stable element

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-elevation>?
decisions.why: documented for custom components (place it in a positioned surface); a stable element

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-badge>?
decisions.why: labs, presentational: renders `value` and has no behaviour or events to go wrong; upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-elevated-card>?
decisions.why: labs, presentational: a styled container with a slot, no properties or events; upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-filled-card>?
decisions.why: labs, presentational: a styled container with a slot, no properties or events; upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-outlined-card>?
decisions.why: labs, presentational: a styled container with a slot, no properties or events; upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-item>?
decisions.why: labs, a layout block with no behaviour: the stable md-list-item renders it (list/internal/listitem/list-item.js), and its declaration documents it for custom list items; upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-navigation-bar>?
decisions.why: labs, but it works as tabs do: role=tablist with arrow, Home, End, Enter and Space handling, and `navigation-bar-activated` reports `activeIndex` (it also fires once on first render, for the initial index); upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-navigation-tab>?
decisions.why: labs, the tab of md-navigation-bar (a role=tab button with `active`, `label` and a badge); the bar finds it through its `navigation-tab-rendered` event; upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-navigation-drawer>?
decisions.why: labs, and wrong for apps: it renders role=dialog for a persistent navigation panel, and `navigation-drawer-changed` fires from an unscoped setTimeout(250) after every change of `opened`, including the first render, not when the transition ends

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-navigation-drawer-modal>?
decisions.why: labs, and not an accessible modal: it renders role=dialog but neither moves focus in on open nor traps it, and Escape closes it only while focus is already inside; md-dialog is the modal surface. Its `navigation-drawer-changed` has md-navigation-drawer's setTimeout(250) problem

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-outlined-segmented-button>?
decisions.why: labs, but sound: a <button aria-pressed> with `selected`, `disabled` and `label`; its `segmented-button-interaction` is how the set hears a click; upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the facade offer <md-outlined-segmented-button-set>?
decisions.why: labs, but sound: role=group, `multiselect`, and `segmented-button-set-selection` reports `index` and `selected` (and the button element, which a view should not keep); upstream is in maintenance mode (README), so labs elements will not graduate or change: kept when its source works as a stable element would

decisions.question: Does the binding offer the event md-sub-menu@request-activation?
decisions.why: md-sub-menu never fires it: it dispatches it on its slotted item (`this.item.dispatchEvent(createRequestActivationEvent())`, menu/internal/submenu/sub-menu.js), where the menu's list navigation handles it; the manifest attributes it to the sub-menu

decisions.question: Which events that upstream elements send each other does the facade offer?
decisions.answer: none: md-assist-chip@update-focus, md-filter-chip@update-focus, md-input-chip@update-focus, md-suggestion-chip@update-focus, md-list-item@request-activation, md-select-option@request-selection, md-select-option@request-deselection, md-sub-menu@activate-typeahead, md-sub-menu@deactivate-items, md-sub-menu@deactivate-typeahead
decisions.why: they coordinate a chip set, a select or a menu with its own items (focus moves, selection requests, typeahead); the containers report the outcome to an app (md-select change, md-menu closed), and offering the internal messages invites a view to depend on them

decisions.question: Which revision of this upstream version is the facade?
decisions.why: engine 0.4.0: the facade is held to @effect/tsgo and the GritQL idioms (its tsconfig.json carries the rules), its changes mounts read an element's state through effect's Record and Array, and its smoke test decodes the page's JSON through Schema
